name: Kenyan Ugali
description: Ugali, a stiff maize porridge, is Kenya's most essential staple starch, eaten daily alongside stews and greens, traditionally torn by hand and used to scoop up other dishes.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring constantly, over medium-low heat 12-15 minutes until very thick, smooth, and pulling away from the sides of the pot.

name: Kenyan Nyama Choma
description: Nyama choma, meaning simply 'roasted meat', is Kenya's most beloved way of preparing meat, traditionally grilled slowly over charcoal and shared communally.
steps_detailed: Rub the beef with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 15 minutes.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, 12-15 minutes, until well charred outside and cooked through.
steps: Rub the beef with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 15 minutes.

name: Kenyan Sukuma Wiki
description: Sukuma wiki, meaning 'to stretch the week' for how far it extends a meal, is Kenya's most common everyday side, built on real collard greens or kale slow-cooked with onion and tomato.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil, 5-6 minutes, then add the tomatoes and simmer 3-4 minutes.
Add the kale and a splash of water, and simmer 10-12 minutes until tender.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil, 5-6 minutes, then add the tomatoes and simmer 3-4 minutes.

name: Kenyan Pilau
description: Pilau, rice cooked in a whole-spice-infused broth, reflects genuine Swahili coastal culinary influence and centuries of Indian Ocean trade.
steps_detailed: Deeply brown the onion in a little oil, 10-12 minutes, until golden.
Add the chicken, cumin, and cinnamon, and brown 6-7 minutes.
Add the rice and broth, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.

name: Kenyan Mandazi
description: Mandazi, lightly sweet, fried coconut-milk dough, is a beloved Kenyan and wider East African snack, especially common at breakfast alongside tea.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, coconut milk, sugar, and baking powder into a soft dough.
Roll out and cut into triangles.
Fry, turning, 3-4 minutes per batch, until deeply golden.

name: Kenyan Chapati
description: Chapati, a soft, layered flatbread, reflects genuine Indian culinary influence and is one of Kenya's most beloved breads, often eaten alongside stews.
steps_detailed: Work the flour with warm water and half the oil into a soft dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Roll thin, brush with the remaining oil, and roll up into a coil before flattening again to build real flaky layers.
Cook in a hot, dry pan, 2-3 minutes per side, until golden with light char spots.

name: Kenyan Githeri
description: Githeri, a simple maize and bean stew, is a genuine Kikuyu staple and one of Kenya's most common everyday one-pot meals.

name: Kenyan Mukimo
description: Mukimo, mashed potato, corn, and greens pounded together into a distinctive green mash, is a genuine Kikuyu specialty.
steps_detailed: Mash the potato, corn, and cooked kale together vigorously until well combined and mostly smooth.
steps: Mash the potato, corn, and cooked kale together vigorously until well combined and mostly smooth.

name: Kenyan Kachumbari
description: Kachumbari, a fresh, finely diced tomato and onion salad, a common East African accompaniment to nyama choma and pilau.
steps_detailed: Toss everything together.

name: Kenyan Chicken Curry
description: A coconut-based chicken curry, reflecting genuine Swahili coastal and Indian culinary influence.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion 4-5 minutes, then add the curry powder, cooking 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and tomatoes, and cook 8-9 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and simmer 12-15 minutes until the chicken is tender.

Cut the phyllo into strips, spoon the filling at one end, and fold into triangles.

Coat the potato slices in the batter and fry, turning, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden.
